title: VAT Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: VAT Calculator: Add or remove VAT at any rate. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [VAT Calculator](/vat-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Add or remove VAT at any rate. Enter your amount, VAT rate and action and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Value Added Tax is a consumption tax used in over 170 countries. This calculator adds VAT to a net price or extracts it from a VAT-inclusive total. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator).

## How to use the VAT Calculator

Start by entering your amount, then entering your VAT rate (%) and finally choosing your action from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your amount.
2. Enter your vat rate (%).
3. Choose your action from the list.
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Add: Gross = Net × (1 + rate). Remove: Net = Gross ÷ (1 + rate).

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [VAT Calculator](/vat-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Adding 20% VAT to 100 gives 120. Removing 20% VAT from 120 gives 100 — not 96. Try the same figures in the [VAT Calculator](/vat-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Amount: 100, VAT rate: 20 %, Action: Add VAT), the [VAT Calculator](/vat-calculator) returns Gross (incl. VAT): 120, VAT: 20, Net (excl. VAT): 100. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Never subtract the VAT percentage from a gross price — divide instead.
- Check reduced rates for food, books and energy.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I remove VAT from a price?

Divide the gross price by 1 + the VAT rate. For 20%, divide by 1.2. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [VAT Calculator](/vat-calculator) and start straight away.

### What is the UK VAT rate?

The UK standard rate is 20%, with reduced rates of 5% and 0% for some goods. Try it with your own numbers in the [VAT Calculator](/vat-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the VAT Calculator use?

Add: Gross = Net × (1 + rate). Remove: Net = Gross ÷ (1 + rate). You can see it in action in the [VAT Calculator](/vat-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the VAT Calculator?

Just Amount, VAT rate and Action. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
